front: TC031: What is the minimum viable move?
back: Before answering under pressure, take one quiet breath and say the first sentence 10–20% slower than your instinct, with a clean stop at the end.

front: TC031: What is the core sequence?
back: Pressure cue -> One breath -> 10–20% slower -> Clean ending -> Choose next move.

front: TC031: What is the field tip?
back: The breath is invisible; the blurt is not.

front: TC031: What is the strong version of: Fast defensive paragraph?
back: One breath. 'I see why it sounded that way. My actual point is...'

front: TC031: What is the strong version of: Instant apology to reduce tension?
back: 'I can own my part without rushing into a yes. The part I would change is...'

front: TC031: What is the strong version of: Over-explaining to a senior person?
back: 'Bottom line first: I recommend X. The main reason is Y.'

front: TC031: What is better than: The same panicked ramble at three-quarter speed?
back: Use the slower pace to choose one sentence — pace and content have to shrink together.

front: TC031: What is better than: Ponderous pauses between every single word?
back: Aim for 10–20% slower — settled, not solemn.

front: TC031: What is better than: 'Yes, fine, I will get it done, can we move on?'?
back: 'Give me a moment — a yes from me needs to mean something.'

front: TC031: What are signs it is working?
back: First sentence feels easier to choose. Other person slows or gets more precise. You say less and answer more directly. Tone sounds clearer, less pleading.

front: TC031: When should you avoid this technique?
back: In casual conversation where a deliberate slow-down reads as unnatural or aloof. When your pace is already appropriate and slowing further would feel laboured.

front: TC031: What is the best recovery line?
back: 'I said yes too quickly. Can I take thirty seconds and answer it properly?'
